To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transcription factor Oleg2, which was previously shown to play a crucial role in the development and maintenance of the oligodendrocyte lineage, is up-regulated in cells of the cerebral cortex in response to brain injury.
the transcription factor Olim2, a repressor of neuronal differentiation in the developing brain, is strongly up-regulated upon brain injuries.
the bHLH factor Olig2 is strongly upregulated after acute and chronic brain injuries, and that Olig2 is a repressor of neuronal differentiation in injured brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the molecular and cellular events that underlie the generation, migration, and differentiation of neural progenitor cells in the adult brain, as well as with the molecular mechanisms that regulate the fate of these progenitor cells in health and disease.
the development of new therapies for the treatment of neurodegenerative and neurotrauma diseases.
the molecular mechanisms of brain injury, and in particular with the mechanisms that control neuronal repair in the adult mammalian CNS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Olig2 transcription factor is a negative regulator of neurogenesis in response to brain injury.
the expression of Olig2, in response to injury, inhibits the differentiation of neural stem cells into neurons and promotes the differentiation into astrocytes.
the expression of Olig2, in response to brain injury, inhibits neurogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transcription factor Oleg2 is a repressor of neuronal repair.
Olig2 is a repressor of neuronal repair in the adult mammalian CNS.
Olig2 is expressed in the brain after injury and that it represses neurogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Olig2 is a negative regulator of neurogenesis in injured brain and that its down regulation is required to allow neuronal repair.
the transcription factor Oleg2 may be a potential target for the induction of endogenous neurogenesis in the context of brain injuries.
we found a transcription factor that can inhibit neurogenesis in the adult brain and can be manipulated to induce neurogenesis.
